clue.text: Point and scoff at old-fashioned garment

parts.note: S is south, one of the compass points
to scoff at is to mock

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a dated piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose overall worn by rural labourers of old is a classic period garment.

clue.text: Grilled cheese may be

explanation.surface: A description of a toasted cheese snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A window fitted with bars is grated, like a grille; cheese is often shredded on a grater.

clue.text: A spell of cricket? Catch and pass

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
to catch is to take

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a bowling spell, a catch and a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is the six-ball spell bowled by one bowler from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a car on the road is to get by it, going ahead.

clue.text: Nothing new about her being shown out

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other here, as a container

parts.note: something that is not new is used
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is escorted out of a place where nothing is new.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher escorts people, so someone guided to the exit has been escorted out.

clue.text: Senior citizen plants tree on isle

parts.note: the alder is a tree
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An elderly person plants a tree on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior citizen' suggests a pensioner but means a senior civic figure on a town council; 'plants' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough council's elder member is a senior figure among a town's citizens.

clue.text: Fence given new colour

parts.note: a pale is a fence stake or paling
green means new or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A fence is repainted in a fresh colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A light shade of the hue of grass is a colour.

clue.text: Is in better position to speak off the cuff

indicators.note: in tells us one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone well placed finds it easier to talk without notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to perform or speak without preparation.

clue.text: Empty vault

explanation.surface: An empty vault in a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear is to empty out; to clear a fence or bar is to vault over it.

clue.text: Fitted top removed from piece of furniture

indicators.note: top removed from tells us to drop the first letter of the furniture word

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A fitted piece of furniture with its top taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fit for a task is capable of it.

clue.text: Second bed delivered without charge

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
to deliver someone is to set them free

explanation.surface: A second bed arrives at no cost to the buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off unpunished or unpaid is to escape with no penalty.

clue.text: Made tea for the family, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word for family is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: a brood is a family of young children

explanation.surface: Someone put the kettle on for the whole household.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is brewed by steeping leaves in hot water.

clue.text: I would abbreviate each proposal

parts.note: I'd is the shortened form of I would

explanation.surface: A suggestion to shorten some words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbreviate' tells us to shorten both I WOULD and EACH, to I'D and EA.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a suggestion or thought put forward.

clue.text: Always increasing?

explanation.surface: A question about whether something keeps growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore is a poetic word for forever; split in two it says growing further all the time.

clue.text: Sort out apples for a dish

indicators.note: sort means arrange the letters of the following words into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sorts apples into a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the phrase 'Sort out' but is anagram fodder with APPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide deep plate for broth is a type of dish.

clue.text: Dad watched, all agog

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: Father looked on, fascinated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wide-eyed with astonishment is agog.

clue.text: Sets aside Tom's battle scars?

explanation.surface: A tomcat's fighting wounds are set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark is to reserve for a purpose; a tomcat fighting gets nicks on its ears.

clue.text: Let bank arrange cover for retirement

indicators.note: arrange means the letters of these words are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bank is asked to arrange a pension plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests a pension, but it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedcovering keeps you warm when you retire for the night.

clue.text: Uplift spiritually?

parts.note: read literally, this means to rise into the air by supernatural means, as at a seance

explanation.definitionFit: To float in the air, supposedly by psychic power, is a spiritual lifting.

clue.text: Where is this sold? Oh, in the local, perhaps

definitions.text: Where is this sold? Oh, in the local, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible rearrangement of the letters of the words around it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where drink is sold and realises it is at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: the local is British slang for one's nearby pub, where drink is sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer, wine and spirits containing intoxicating spirit are sold in pubs.

clue.text: Thumbs up for it

parts.note: a raised thumb is the gesture given to something one is in favour of

explanation.definitionFit: Giving the thumbs up is a gesture of endorsement.

clue.text: Six ways to watch television?

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
E and W, east and west, are directions or ways

explanation.surface: Six different ways to watch TV.
explanation.definitionFit: To view is to watch, and TV audiences are called viewers.

clue.text: Refuse to allow a free vote

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a free vote in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a formal block of a proposal, refusing it.

clue.text: Unfortunate American soldier trapped in overturned vehicle

indicators.note: trapped in means one piece sits inside another
overturned in a down clue means the vehicle word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US soldier is caught in a vehicle that has rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' suits a down clue, where the vehicle reads upwards; 'trapped in' puts the soldier inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calamitous or unlucky is disastrous.

clue.text: Smooth sort of crossing

explanation.surface: A road meets a railway smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth means flat and even; a road meets a railway at a level crossing.

clue.text: Lorraine's companion in France

parts.note: the region of eastern France paired with Lorraine in a historic double name

explanation.definitionFit: Alsace-Lorraine is the region annexed by Germany in 1871, two French provinces named together.

clue.text: Abroad, went out in old hat

parts.note: out means away or abroad
to date someone is to go out with them

explanation.surface: Someone abroad wore an antique hat on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something no longer in fashion.

clue.text: Post the money for the pools entry?

definitions.text: the money for the pools entry?

explanation.surface: Sending off cash for a football pools coupon.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is a wooden post; it is also the sum wagered, as on a British football pools coupon.

clue.text: Goods carrier on certain trips

indicators.note: trips means the letters stumble and fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lorry carries goods on certain journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: A large steel box carries freight by ship or lorry.
